question: Mahatma Gandhi gave the slogan of ‘Do or Die’ during the ___________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Quit India Movement**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Mahatma Gandhi gave the slogan of **'Do or Die'** during the **Quit India Movement**__.
 
• The Quit India Movement was launched on **8th August 1942**, during World War II, demanding an end to British rule in India.
 
• It was a mass protest demanding what Gandhi called "an orderly British withdrawal" from India.
 
• The movement saw widespread acts of defiance and protests, including strikes, demonstrations, and the refusal to pay taxes.
 
• Despite the arrest of major leaders, the movement continued with the active participation of the masses, showcasing the strong desire for independence.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• The Quit India Movement is also known as the **August Kranti** or August Movement.
 
• The British government responded with mass detentions and suppression of the movement, but it marked a significant phase in the Indian independence struggle.
 
• Gandhi's call for "Do or Die" motivated millions of Indians to participate actively in the freedom struggle, leading to a significant impact on the British decision to eventually leave India.
 
• The movement demonstrated the unity and determination of the Indian people to achieve self-rule and independence.
